title: A lane reads a PR's merge state right after opening it, because a dirty PR gets no CI run
why: Lesson 2 of 4 from lane priority-vs-merge-order (04:04 CST Nov 14, relayed; the lane's read, unchecked by triage): a PR whose merge state is dirty (a conflict with its base) gets no CI run, so a lane that does not read the state after opening waits on a run that never starts. Coordinator 04:05 CST found no step that owns this (read from step titles on origin/roadmap 78da521a2, not bodies). Triage grep of step file names for "merge-state" and "dirty" found none. Check idea (unbuilt): the opening act or the handoff reads the PR's merge state and says "dirty" in its output. Owner-visible effect: a lane stops waiting on a run that cannot start.
note: Filed 04:06 CST Nov 14 by triage. Tracker: the coordinator. Path ALONE. No lane yet.
